Title: Ummo Indera Mahkota chief's home among 2 houses destroyed in Kuantan fire
Article:
KUANTAN: The home of Umno Indera Mahkota division chief Datuk Mustaffar Kamal Ab Hamid was among two double-storey terrace houses involved in a fire at Taman Seri Kuantan here tonight.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department Operations and Rescue Division assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the department received an emergency call at 7.26pm.
He said 36 firefighters from the Kuantan, Indera Mahkota and Gebeng fire and rescue stations were deployed to the scene.
"The fire involved two houses, but no casualties were reported. Firefighting operations are still underway, while the cause of the fire is under investigation," he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, Umno Indera Mahkota division deputy chief Muhammad Faiz Hashim urged Mustaffar Kamal to remain patient and strong in facing the ordeal.
"Be patient and stay strong, Datuk Ketua Bahagian (Mustaffar Kamal), in facing this test," he wrote in a post on Threads.

Title: More women contact UK police after Russell Brand rape case
Article:
LONDON: More women have come forward since the start of Russell Brand's rape and assault trial, a UK police chief said Tuesday, as the disgraced TV star began a 10-year jail sentence.
The reports of fresh complaints came as Brand's defence lawyer faced a storm of criticism for his comments and line of questioning in court, reopening the debate about victim shaming in Britain.
Detective Inspector Andy Furphy from the London Metropolitan Police said two further allegations against Brand were already being investigated and "we've had several reports in during the trial and since the verdict" on Thursday.
Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, was on Monday jailed for 10 years and six months after being found guilty of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009.
The judge described him as a "sexual predator" who had shown "staggering arrogance" and "contempt" for his victims.
But defence lawyer Ian Winter has been sharply criticised for telling the trial Brand's victims were "not particularly vulnerable at all" and that he could not be guilty of rape as his accusers had not "resisted or screamed or even tried to leave."
UK deputy prime minister Lucy Powell said she found some of the defence's comments at the trial "incredibly depressing."
Support organisations said such tactics harked back to a previous era when victims were reluctant to come forward for fear of being quizzed in court on their behaviour and sexual history.
Victim Support said it had been "appalled, but not surprised, by the rape myths, misconceptions and stereotypes deployed by the defence" during Brand's trial.
It added that women should not have had to endure "disgraceful attempts to blame and discredit them" in court.
"Rape myths and stereotypes are still used day in, day out in sexual violence trials. The defendant's profile in this case has shone a spotlight on a systemic failing faced by victim-survivors across the country," it said.
Brand was charged last year after being exposed in 2023 by journalists from the Sunday Times, The Times and the Channel 4 Dispatches programme, leading to women coming forward to make complaints to police.
"Throughout Russell Brand's trial, we saw rape myths in action: Why didn't she scream? Why didn't she fight back?
"Why did she wait so long to report it? Why did she maintain contact with him afterwards?" wrote Ciara Bergman, head of Rape Crisis England & Wales, in The iPaper after Brand's conviction.
"These were all introduced as ways of discrediting the survivors and/or introducing doubt into the minds of jurors," she said.
Bergman, however, added the guilty verdict on the rape charge was "important" as the complainant had earlier had consensual sex with Brand.
"It suggests understanding among jurors that there is no such thing as blanket or automatic consent," she said.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Saturday the government must look at changing rape trials to "make sure they do not leave the woman feeling like she is on trial in court as has been the experience of people in the past."
Describing Brand's actions as "horrifying", he pledged to introduce specialist rape and serious sexual offence teams in every police force by the end of 2027.
Rights of Women said the Brand trial highlighted the "urgent need for a trauma-informed justice system."
Giving evidence in court often meant women who had already "experienced significant trauma" were "re-victimised by the processes that should bring them both safety and justice", it said.

Title: Egypt's military has been in Saudi for months, says FM
Article:
CAIRO: Egypt has had a military presence in Saudi Arabia for months, Cairo's top diplomat has said, two weeks after its parliament authorised helping defend the kingdom from Houthi attacks.
Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said Egypt was now "strengthening" the deployment, which had not previously been announced.
"We have already military presence there upon request from our brothers and sisters in Saudi Arabia," Abdelatty said in an interview with France24 aired on Monday, adding: "We are strengthening that."
Last month, Egypt's parliament approved President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request to send military support to Saudi Arabia, which is under regular attack from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.
It wasn't clear whether lawmakers knew of the existing military presence. At the time, lawmakers told AFP they had not received details about the scale or size of the planned deployment.
"Our presence there (began) a few months ago after the attacks and aggressions on Saudi Arabia during the escalation with Iran," Abdelatty said, without giving further details.
He said Egypt's coming deployment was for "defensive objectives", including "air defence capabilities to defend the different sensitive sites in Saudi Arabia, including of course the holy sites and others."
Makkah and Madinah, Islam's holiest cities, are in western Saudi Arabia. Saudi authorities have accused the Houthis of attacks in the area, which they deny.
Abdelatty, who was speaking in Paris during a visit for the G7 foreign ministers' meeting, also downplayed a comment from a member of the Houthi politburo who, after Egypt's parliamentary approval, said the move was a declaration of war.
"If you recall, another senior Houthi official said (that they) appreciate and welcome any role from Egypt to mediate and de-escalate. This is what we are trying to do, because there is no military solution."
Riyadh – one of Cairo's closest allies and a key financial backer of Sisi's administration – has not publicly commented on Egypt's potential involvement.
Facing near-daily attacks by Yemen's Houthis, Saudi Arabia has received military support from allies including the United Kingdom, which has pledged fighter jets, and France, which has said it would help defend oil infrastructure.

Title: #NSTViral: Trailer carrying backhoe, container truck collide on NKVE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A collision involving a trailer carrying a backhoe and a container truck along the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) towards Setia Alam left debris scattered across the carriageway, with motorists seen manoeuvring around the wreckage.
A New Straits Times check with the PlusLine hotline confirmed that the accident occurred at KM13.9 of the highway at about 7.15pm today.
The incident was also highlighted in a post on Threads by user fazrilhaikal, who claimed that the trailer had hit a flyover because the backhoe exceeded the height limit.
"The trailer carrying a backhoe hit the flyover because it exceeded the height limit," he wrote.
Other users raised questions about the circumstances of the collision, with one suggesting that a billboard might have been involved after noticing what appeared to be debris falling from above.
Another user, mrdhhmhmmd, said the incident reinforced their fear of driving alongside container trucks.
"An old fear proven right. I've always felt nervous driving alongside container trucks. This is exactly why," the user wrote.

Title: Bulgaria motorway pileup kills 12, injures dozens
Article:
SOFIA: Twelve people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup in thick fog on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU.
Crashes snared around 50 cars and trucks heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency.
Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles, at the scene of the accident near the city of Yambol.
Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev said in a statement that a sudden change in weather conditions was the main reason for the pileup.
Visibility was around 70-80 metres immediately before the incident, but dropped to approximately 10 metres within a short period, according to information available to the ministry.
"We are actively working on equipping the toll system gantries with display screens to warn drivers," he said.
The motorway section should have been closed early Tuesday, Bogdan Milchev, chairman of the Road Safety Institute NGO, told public radio station BNR, blaming the government.
Eleven people died at the scene, while another person died after being admitted to hospital, the health ministry said in a statement.
In total, 51 people were admitted to hospitals in nearby cities, with 13 of them critically injured, it added.
The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams, as government officials rushed to the scene, while Prime Minister Rumen Radev cancelled his appointments for later Tuesday.
The government wants Wednesday to be a day of national mourning, while President Iliana Iotova, rushing back from abroad, also expressed her condolences.
Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures.
Victims blame the Balkan nation's high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system.
Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed "deepest condolences" to the victims and their families in a post on X.
European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was "deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning."
A total of 456 people were killed in road traffic accidents in Bulgaria in 2025 – down five per cent from the previous year and 27 per cent lower than in 2019.
In 2019, the EU introduced a target to reduce road deaths and serious injuries by 50 per cent by 2030.
A European Commission report in October said that although the EU remains "one of the world's safest regions for road travel", the majority of member states were not yet on track to meet the safety target.
The report said that just five of the EU's 27 countries – including Bulgaria – were on track to meet the target.
In 2023, Bulgaria's parliament adopted stricter penalties for anyone found to be driving under the influence of drugs.
The cars of accused drivers are now impounded until the trial, even when the suspects have no previous criminal record.
Bulgaria's busy road traffic due to its position as a gateway to the EU is one of the main factors behind the high accident rate, according to experts.
But Bulgaria's status as the EU's poorest member state also plays a role, with around half of the cars registered being more than 20 years old.

Title: Greta Thunberg slams UN climate COPs as 'greenwashed circuses'
Article:
ANTALYA: Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg on Tuesday criticised the UN's annual climate summits as "greenwashed circuses", as she arrived in Turkiye for the COP31 conference.
Many of Thunberg's fellow climate activists have become disillusioned with a process which has yielded few major breakthroughs in recent years, with fossil fuel-producing nations often holding up proceedings and action on cutting emissions.
"COPs have become greenwashed circuses. That is the reality," Thunberg, who had not taken part in the climate conferences since Glasgow in 2021, told the press and throng who had gathered for her arrival.
"Of course it is absolutely crucial that we still do everything we possibly can because this is an opportunity to mobilise people," she said after arriving late to the talks in Antalya.
"We are here as activists to push those people in power to actually implement what they have been talking about for decades and decades," she added.
"The climate disasters that we have seen recently (are) something that scientists and people living on the front lines have been warning about for decades."
"And we also need to acknowledge that the COPs are not sufficient to prevent a climate catastrophe."
Observers expect few significant developments from COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia's conflict in Ukraine.

Title: KLIA to hold aviation security exercise on Thursday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Eagle Stealth Safety Exercise to test the country's preparedness and response capabilities in handling aviation security threats will be held at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 on Thursday.
The National Security Council (NSC), under the Prime Minister's Department, said the exercise would run from 9am to 11.30pm and was being conducted in collaboration with Malaysia Airports.
It said the exercise aimed to assess preparedness levels, inter-agency coordination and the effectiveness of the national response mechanism in addressing civil aviation security threats.
"Flight operations will continue as usual and this exercise will not affect flight services or operations at KLIA," it said in a statement.
NSC advised members of the public around KLIA Terminal 1 to remain calm if they witnessed the movement of security personnel, operational assets or training activities during the exercise.
"There is no actual threat. All activities conducted are purely simulations for training purposes," it said.

Title: Embattled Pentagon chief slams impeachment 'farce'
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday denounced a push to impeach him as a "farce" and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under President Donald Trump.
"It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it," he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the impeachment push "slander" and "sabotage."
Hegseth's combative performance came as Congress inched toward a rare vote on impeachment over alleged misconduct related to wars against Iran and Yemen's Houthis, and the controversial killing of alleged drug smugglers in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.
The effort throws down a challenge to Trump, already weakened by last week's midterms drubbing, where anger at the sputtering Iran war and subsequent surge in fuel prices helped drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.
Trump has acknowledged that the Iran war contributed to his party losing both the House and Senate in Congress.
But moments after Hegseth's televised press conference, the 80-year-old president signalled his backing.
"Pete Hegseth gets an 'A' PLUS, PLUS, PLUS," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
The expected vote in the House comes in the lame duck period when Republicans still retain their narrow majority, ahead of next January when the huge new Democratic majority takes over.
If a majority in the House voted in favour, the Senate would still need a two thirds majority to convict and remove Hegseth – a tall order even after Democrats take up power there too in January.
The impeachment articles have been introduced by a Republican Trump critic, Thomas Massie, who will exit Congress after losing his seat.
Trump called Massie "a disgruntled, angry, defeated former Congressman" and "a TOTAL LOSER!"
Hegseth defended the operations in Yemen, Iran, Venezuela and against alleged drug smugglers.
"I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow," he said, also seeking to equate the effort to remove him with an attack on US troops.
"These resolutions tell every one of them that their service was a crime. Their service was not a crime. These are heroes," said Hegseth.
Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on US military interventions.
Hegseth has called the widely unpopular war a "courageous and historic effort."
The 2025 conflict with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis also features in Massie's articles of impeachment, which charge Hegseth with starting the operation without congressional approval and in the absence of an imminent threat to the United States.
Massie also branded strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific as "extrajudicial killings" and said Hegseth "chilled independent legal review within the Department of Defence."
And he accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video in which he and other lawmakers urged military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders.
For Hegseth, the articles of impeachment amount to an attack on Trump's record, which he said he is happy to defend.
"If they want to talk about... President Trump's foreign policy and national security record, let's do it. I'll see you there. Let's have a conversation about the success that I outlined here," Hegseth said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From Fox News to Pentagon chief, Hegseth faces fight for survival
Article:
PETE  Hegseth, a former National Guard officer who went from Fox News co-host to leading the world's most powerful military, is fighting to keep his job less than two years into his tenure as Pentagon chief.
The 46-year-old has survived a series of controversies as defence secretary, but many resurfaced in the articles of impeachment introduced on Monday by Thomas Massie, a Republican opponent of President Donald Trump who wants to remove Hegseth from office.
Hegseth said he was ready to defend his record.
"I couldn't be more proud of what our president has done, the decisions that he's made, the courageous calls that he's made, the bold nature of our... military leadership, the skill and courage of the troops on the ground," he said.
Hegseth, 46, has sought to transform the  War Department — as Trump has unofficially renamed the Defence Department.
Deploying a combative and aggressive style, he has relentlessly targeted diversity, equity and inclusion efforts at the Pentagon and has fought to kick transgender troops out of the military and to bar others from joining.
"We are no longer the 'woke' department, or the weak department," said Hegseth in characteristically colourful remarks to troops earlier this year.
"No fatties, no trannies, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals.
"Just warriors — just tough, ready, committed troops."
Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on and oversight of United States military interventions.
Hegseth is a vehement defender of the grinding, open-ended and widely unpopular conflict, which he has described as a "courageous and historic effort".
The Iran conflict was the fifth major international US military intervention under Hegseth, but unlike the first four, the war against Teheran has been neither quick nor bloodless from the American side, and has also wreaked economic havoc around the globe.
Heavily-tattooed Hegseth is a former infantry officer who spent more than 18 years in the National Guard and served in combat, deploying to Iraq and Afghanistan, and he often posts social media clips of himself working out with troops.
But he had no experience heading a large organisation before leading the Pentagon.
He came under fire during his confirmation process over alleged financial mismanagement at veterans' non-profits where he previously worked, as well as reports of excessive drinking and allegations of sexually assaulting a woman in California.
A few months after he took office, the
Atlantic
magazine revealed that its editor-in-chief was inadvertently included in a Signal chat in which Hegseth and other officials discussed imminent strikes on Yemen, with the Pentagon chief sending messages on the timing of the operation hours before it began.
Strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific have also been a source of controversy, especially an attack last year that left survivors who were killed in a follow-up strike.
Massie branded those attacks "extrajudicial killings" and said Hegseth "chilled independent
legal review within the  Defence Department".
In another contentious move under Hegseth, a number of senior military personnel, including the top-ranking general Charles "CQ" Brown, have been fired, often with little or no public explanation.
Hegseth has insisted that Trump is simply choosing the leaders he wants, but Democratic lawmakers have raised concerns about politicisation of the traditionally neutral US military.
The defence chief,  in a December 2025 speech, said the Pentagon "will not be distracted by democracy-building interventionism, undefined wars, regime change, climate change, woke moralising and feckless nation building".
"We will deter war. We will advance our interests. We will defend our people. Peace is our goal," he told the Reagan National Defence Forum.
But in January, US forces
seized Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro and his wife in a shock raid in the capital Caracas.
Less than two months later, the US and Israel launched their war against Iran, a conflict that has since spread to countries around the Middle East.
Critics say the Iran war is the kind of military campaign Hegseth repeatedly denounced, but is now pursuing.
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Restore academic freedom to revive Malaysia's university excellence
Article:
MALAYSIAN scholarship  in the 1960s was fertile ground for academic titans like Tan Chee Khoon, Royal Professor Datuk Ungku Abdul Aziz  and Professor Datuk Syed Hussein Al-Attas.
They were key to Malaysian universities becoming  centres of intellectual rigour and critical debate while maintaining institutional autonomy.  These figures bestrode Malaysian academia like rock stars, and the stature they attained during the post-Merdeka social revolution, notably at Universiti Malaya, has never been replicated.
In their heyday, UM's University Council, chaired by Tan, a legendary former member of parliament known popularly as "Mr Opposition", reflected left-leaning radicalism with an anti-colonial bent.   Under Tan, the council leadership was shaped by merit and democratic representation, rather than political loyalty.
Instead of hiding away in ivory towers, they engaged in nation-building and criticised government policies while spearheading public discourse and powering socioeconomic reforms.
This intellectual bravado and hotbed of activism declined after the May 13, 1969 racial riots, particularly after the enactment of the Universities and University Colleges Act (Auku )in  1971.
Varsity budgets became strained, forcing  decades of over-reliance on commercial partnerships or student-driven revenue.   This led to a lack of specialised equipment, advanced research software and comprehensive digital resources.
Brain drain and a culture of mediocrity then resulted in our universities suffering in global rankings. After decades of pushback, the dons are now calling for academic freedom and better welfare in the proposed repeal of  Auku.
There is opportunity now for universities to phase out unfair promotions and favouritism, and practices that undermine morale and meritocracy.   Performance appraisals must recognise teaching, research, post-graduate supervision and societal contributions.
The proposed One Higher Education Act aims for fairer treatment, stronger grievance mechanisms and better accountability. Political appointments should be replaced with independent, peer-reviewed and merit-based ones.   Faculty leaders must regain autonomy to manage curricula, departmental policies and student engagement.
Red tape  must be slashed to focus on impactful research and mentorship. Funding should be directed towards competitive, programme-based grants, building better digital infrastructure, securing access to international scholarly databases and modernising laboratory facilities.
Eventually, the reforms should create public discourse without career-ending consequences. These reforms must also plug the  brain drain by improving compensation, restoring critical thought and paving a transparent path for  career advancement.
Ultimately, the overhaul must aim to recreate the halcyon years of the Tans, Ungku Azizes and Syed Husseins.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nvidia's Huang scandal rattles AI industry built around him
Article:
NVIDIA chief executive officer  Jensen Huang sits at the centre of the artificial intelligence  boom, and the spy scandal that erupted over the weekend threatens to shake the company at  a time when confidence in the AI investment frenzy is already fragile.
Taiwan-born Huang is regarded as the godfather of the AI economy, the executive every player in the industry must turn to because the technology depends on the graphics processing units (GPUs) that his company designs.
Those chips have made Nvidia one of the two most valuable companies in the world, alongside Apple.
GPUs are in short supply, and the most powerful tech executives and companies rely on Huang to keep them flowing to the data centres that run the models behind OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude.
Huang has also plowed Nvidia's windfall into AI startups and labs that spend the money on his chips, a circular arrangement that could spread any trouble at Nvidia across the industry.
"Nvidia without Jensen — I don't know what that's worth," Stephen Witt, author of a book on Huang and Nvidia, told CNBC. "Nvidia is Jensen Huang."
The scandal over Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy lands days before Anthropic's expected initial public offering, a Wall Street offering seen as a key test for an industry under pressure as investors show more caution in the AI story.
That wariness was fuelled by last week's United States elections, in which voters showed anger at AI, tech billionaires and the data centres that house Nvidia's chips.
Silicon Valley figures rallied to Huang's defence.
Shaun Maguire, a partner at Sequoia Capital, wrote on X that Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that "was bad for America", but said he believed there had been no bad intention and that Huang was "irreplaceable for America's AI leadership".
"I simply do not believe he would ever knowingly do anything to disadvantage either America or Nvidia," said investor Gavin Baker, who has known Huang for almost 30 years.
Other investors were less confident Huang would survive the probe launched by the Nvidia board.
"I doubt Jensen Huang will be able to remain as Nvidia CEO," wrote Gary Black of the Future Fund, which counts Nvidia among its largest holdings, adding that Huang had "no natural successor within the company".
Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co called it "a black eye moment" for Huang and said the Nvidia chief was "the core DNA of Nvidia".
"Jensen is not replaceable," said Ives, adding that he expected Huang to remain CEO in the near term but that the board's findings could still lead to his removal.
Huang's fate will likely be determined in Washington.
Ives said the scandal would spark multiple congressional inquiries and increase scrutiny of chip sales to China, a sensitive issue as the AI race between the US and China accelerates.
Huang had persuaded the Trump administration to ease restrictions on chip sales to China and, after donating to some White House causes, became a close adviser to President Donald Trump.
But Democrats won control of Congress in last week's elections, and China hawks from both parties are expected to ask why Trump did not act  when he was first told of Huang's ties to the Chinese business-woman now suspected of spying for Beijing.
Bill Bishop, author of the Sinocism newsletter on China, said Huang's role in deciding who gets Nvidia's scarce chips made him a valuable target.
"With the new Congress, expect subpoenas and public hearings in which he is trashed and he and Nvidia are further damaged," Bishop wrote.
The scandal was "a win" for China's State Security Ministry, and Huang will now pay the consequences, he concluded.
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dozens of foreigners' deaths go undetected in Greece, researchers say
Article:
ATHENS: More than 100 foreign nationals have died since 2000 in Greek police stations or migrant centres with inadequate healthcare facilities, including 34 deaths that have not been officially registered, according to research published on Tuesday by Oxford University researchers.
In total, the research found 112 deaths in the 26-year period, including 44 suicides.
Of the 112 deaths, 84 occurred in police stations without medical staff and 27 were reported in migrant detention facilities.
The Greek government and the police ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The dataset, part of an ongoing project that monitors deaths of foreign nationals in detention, including those held on criminal grounds, draws on police statistics obtained through freedom of information requests, international monitoring reports, media and testimonies.
The findings reveal "gaps in official police records and serious barriers to healthcare, including in facilities receiving EU funding," the report's authors said in a statement.
They said 34 deaths documented by journalists, NGOs and monitors were not included in the police statistics.
The data, published on research platform Detention Landscapes, reflects complaints by human rights groups and follows a 2026 report by the Council of Europe's anti-torture committee (CPT).
The report said that deaths in police custody in Greece had increased and some could have been prevented with sufficient supervision, psychiatric care and healthcare.
Among the cases it examined was the death of a 37-year-old Pakistani migrant while in detention at an Athens police station.
The CPT also cited persistent overcrowding in prison cells, including five people in spaces meant for one, and detainees sleeping on concrete or bedbug-infested mattresses.
Greece, long a landing point for migrants trying to enter the European Union from Africa, Asia and the Middle East, told the CPT that it was taking steps to address deficiencies under a 2025-2030 action plan to improve detention conditions, protect prisoners' rights, boost staff and ease prison overcrowding, a problem in over 60 per cent of countries worldwide, according to a 2024 UN report.

Title: Taiwan suspends investment talks with Malaysia over Anwar's remarks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Taiwan has confirmed that it suspended bilateral investment negotiations with Malaysia last month following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's remarks describing Taiwan as part of China.
United Daily News, in its report, quoted Taiwan's Foreign Ministry spokesman Hsiao Kuang-wei saying the decision was made in consideration of the island's national sovereignty and economic security, as well as to safeguard the interests of Taiwanese investors.
Hsiao was responding to reports by Nikkei Asia that Taiwan had called off bilateral trade talks with Malaysia scheduled for late October.
He said the ministry had expressed serious concern over Anwar's "unfriendly" remarks in August, warning that they could undermine Taiwanese businesses' confidence in investing in Malaysia and expose them to greater risks.
Hsiao said Taiwan had temporarily suspended the investment negotiations to protect its investors, but continued to engage with Kuala Lumpur in the hope of creating favourable conditions for their resumption.
Nikkei Asia's report said that diplomatic tensions between the two sides could jeopardise future Taiwanese investments in Malaysia, particularly in the semiconductor industry.
It cited a Malaysian government source claiming that talks to expand bilateral trade cooperation, scheduled for late October, had been put on hold following Anwar's remarks.
Anwar sparked controversy during an interview with Al Jazeera in August when he said he considered Taiwan part of China.
In the interview, Anwar expressed support for the One China policy, stating that historical factors should be considered when examining Taiwan's relationship with China, while adding that Taiwan was part of China and the matter should ultimately be left to the Chinese people.
The comments drew a strong reaction from Taiwan's Foreign Ministry, which accused Anwar of making "false" statements that suggested Taiwan was a breakaway province of China, while openly rationalising Beijing's position on the use of force to achieve reunification.
Nikkei Asia also reported that Taiwanese business leaders were increasingly concerned about the diplomatic fallout.
Taiwan Chamber of Commerce in Malaysia honorary president Lin Kai-min was quoted as saying that existing operations were unlikely to be immediately affected as companies had already committed substantial capital, but investors were becoming more cautious about new projects and expansion plans.
Lin warned that geopolitical uncertainty could prompt Taiwanese companies, particularly those serving European and United States markets, to reconsider future investment locations amid concerns over supply chain security, technology protection and export control compliance.
The report also quoted Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) president William Ng cautioning that future investments could shift to Vietnam or Thailand if Malaysia's perceived neutrality changed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar rallies behind Aina Abdul ahead of Eurovision Asia debut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has sent words of encouragement to singer Aina Abdul, who will represent Malaysia at the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand, on Nov 14.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said Aina's participation demonstrated that Malaysian talent and creative works could reach greater heights and compete on the international stage.
"Certainly, all Malaysians are proud of this achievement," he said.
He also expressed hope that Aina would deliver her best performance with confidence and determination.
"All the best to Aina Abdul, who will represent Malaysia at the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand. Win or lose, Aina will always be our pride. Fly high, Aina!" he said.
Aina's selection as Malaysia's representative was announced during the 40th Anugerah Juara Lagu (AJL40) on Aug 15.
The singer will perform her song 'Bluest Sky' at the competition, which will feature contestants from 11 Asian countries, including Malaysia.
According to the performance order announced by the organisers on Oct 29, Aina is scheduled to be the 11th and final contestant to perform.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Seven arrested over firecrackers set off on Skudai road
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested three more men in connection with an incident in which firecrackers were set off on a road near the Taman Nesa traffic lights in Skudai, which went viral on social media two days ago.
Johor Baru North police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrol Anuar Nor said the arrests, made about 4.30am today, brought the total number of suspects detained to seven, with six expected to be charged at the Magistrate's Court here tomorrow.
"In a raid around Skudai, we arrested three men aged between 19 and 23 and seized several items to assist in the investigation," he said in a statement today.
He said two of the three latest suspects had previous criminal and drug records, but preliminary urine screening tests found that all three were free from drugs.
Earlier, four men aged between 16 and 25 were arrested about 7.30pm two days ago and remanded for three days until tomorrow.

Title: Public told to avoid river activities during monsoon season
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The public has been advised to postpone all water recreational activities, including bathing, swimming, picnicking and camping, at rivers, rapids, waterfalls and irrigation canals throughout the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon season.
In a statement, the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department said unpredictable weather conditions, coupled with heavy and prolonged rainfall in several areas, could cause sudden rises in water levels, strong currents and water surges, posing serious risks to public safety.
"Water surges can occur in the blink of an eye. Do not wait until the current becomes strong before taking action. Safety and the preservation of life must always be the priority," it said.
The department reminded the public to stay alert to weather developments, follow instructions from the authorities and take preventive measures to avoid untoward incidents.
"In the event of an emergency, the public should immediately call the 999 emergency hotline and provide the location of the incident to rescue personnel," it said.
The department also conveyed its condolences and sympathies to the families of victims involved in a water surge incident at Sungai Pertak, Kuala Kubu Bharu, Selangor, yesterday.
Eight people were reported to have been swept away by strong currents while engaging in recreational and hiking activities in the surrounding area.
Another 26 people who were stranded near the incident site were rescued by emergency response teams.
"This incident serves as another serious reminder that recreational activities in rivers and forest areas carry significant safety risks, particularly during unpredictable weather conditions throughout the monsoon season," JBPM said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Local authority officer held over alleged RM26,000 bribes
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a local authority officer suspected of soliciting and accepting about RM26,000 in bribes from the owner of a runner service company.
The payments were allegedly made in exchange for expediting the issuance of business licences and refraining from taking enforcement action against the company.
A source said the male suspect, in his 30s, was arrested about 10.30am today when he turned up at the Selangor MACC office to give a statement.
"Initial investigations found that the suspect allegedly committed the offences between 2019 and 2023.
"The suspect is believed to have received the bribes through several fund transfers into his personal bank account," the source said.
Selangor MACC director Mohd Azwan Ramli confirmed the arrest, saying the case was being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009.

Title: Kelantan Bersatu chief confirms dismissal as state exco
Article:
KOTA BARU: Kelantan Bersatu chairman Datuk Kamaruddin Md Nor has confirmed receiving a letter terminating his appointment as the state executive councillor for tourism, culture, arts and heritage.
In a brief telephone conversation with the New Straits Times, Kamaruddin said he received the letter from the state government today.
"What I can confirm is that I received the letter today, but I will not reveal the details now.
"I will speak about it during a press conference tomorrow," he said.
Kamaruddin, who is the Ayer Lanas assemblyman, however, said the decision would not affect the party.
Yesterday, Kamaruddin said he was aware of rumours surrounding his possible termination but had yet to receive any official letter from the state government.
Kamaruddin has served as a state exco member since August 2023.
He has also helmed Kelantan Bersatu for the past 10 years.
The decision by the Pas-led state government is believed to have been made amid the ongoing political rift between Pas and Bersatu, the two main parties in Perikatan Nasional (PN), following the breakdown of their political cooperation.
The strained relationship between the parties escalated in May when Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang announced that the party would re-evaluate its cooperation with Bersatu over several issues, including alleged differences in political direction and the handling of internal party matters.
On June 8, Pas announced its decision to terminate all political cooperation with Bersatu following a special meeting of its central working committee.
The move raised questions over the future of Bersatu representatives holding positions in Pas-led state governments, including Kelantan.
It is also learnt that Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud will hold a special press conference on the matter tomorrow.

Title: Najib arrives at Taman Duta home to begin house arrest [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrived at his residence in Taman Duta here at 9.27pm tonight to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
The former Pekan member of parliament was transported in a silver Proton X70 sports utility vehicle (SUV), accompanied by several vehicles from the Prisons Department and the police.
His arrival was met by dozens of local and international media personnel who had been waiting outside the residence since as early as 9am.
Several police and Prisons Department vehicles were also stationed around the residence as part of security arrangements.
Earlier today, the High Court ordered Najib to serve the remainder of his reduced six-year prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence, with immediate effect.
High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after setting aside an order issued against Najib by the High Court Criminal Registry on Nov 6.
Under the order, Najib will remain under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, before returning to Kajang Prison on Aug 24, 2028, to serve his separate prison sentence in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.
Following the ruling, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the Home Ministry was ready to implement the court's decision.
He said the ministry had always respected the conditional royal pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
Saifuddin Nasution said the earlier delay in implementation was due to legal questions surrounding the interpretation of the conditional pardon and the implications of the Nov 6 order.
He said the High Court's latest decision had clarified those questions, adding that the ministry and the Prisons Department would ensure that all decisions concerning detention and sentence enforcement were carried out in accordance with the law and valid court orders.
Najib's lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, earlier described the former prime minister as relieved by the ruling, saying he had been waiting for the house arrest arrangement.
Shafee also thanked Sultan Ibrahim for granting Najib the conditional royal pardon.

Article:

laboratory analysis

Title: Penang industrialisation pioneer Chet Singh dies at 90
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Former Penang Development Corporation (PDC) general manager Datuk Seri Chet Singh Karam Singh, widely regarded as one of the architects of Penang's industrialisation, died this morning. He was 90.
His death was confirmed by his daughter, Surita Amreeth Karamsingh, when contacted.
Chet Singh's passing marks the end of an era for a man who, alongside the late former chief minister Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu, played a pivotal role in transforming Penang into the 'Silicon Valley of the East'.
Born in Kuala Kangsar, Perak, in 1936, Chet began his civil service career at the Defence Ministry before being appointed Penang State Financial Officer in late 1967.
Following the establishment of PDC after Penang lost its free port status, Chet was seconded to lead the corporation.
He served as its general manager for 20 years, from 1971 until his retirement in 1991.
Under his leadership, Penang underwent a rapid transformation from a state grappling with severe unemployment following the loss of its port status into an export-oriented industrial hub.
He played a key role in attracting multinational semiconductor companies, including National Semiconductor, AMD, Hewlett-Packard and Intel, to establish their pioneering offshore manufacturing operations in the Bayan Lepas Free Trade Zone.
By the time he retired in 1991, the state's industrial parks housed more than 500 manufacturing companies employing over 115,000 workers, reversing the economic decline and raising Penang's per capita income well above the national average.
According to a bereavement notice shared by Gurdwara Sahib Bayan Baru, the wake will be held tomorrow from 9.30am at his residence in Minden Heights, Gelugor.
Family members and friends may pay their final respects before the cortege departs at 2.15pm.
The funeral and last rites (saskar) will be held at the Batu Gantung Crematorium at 3pm.

Title: Expired import permit leads to seizure of 25 tonnes of frozen chicken
Article:
BUKIT KAYU HITAM: Nearly 25 tonnes of frozen chicken worth RM562,290 were seized by the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) after the importer was found to have submitted an expired import permit.
The seizure followed a physical inspection by MCBA officers at the Bilik Sejuk Beli, Block E1, Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex, yesterday.
The inspection found that the frozen chicken products, categorised as 'Chicken Thigh & Leg Boneless Frozen', had been imported from Thailand.
Further checks revealed that the importer had submitted an import permit issued by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) that had expired.
The consignment was seized under Section 11(1) of the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Act 2011 (Act 728).
The case was referred to MAQIS for further action.
MCBA Bukit Kayu Hitam commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Fauzi Mohd Yusof said the agency would not compromise on any violation of the law, particularly involving imports that failed to meet the stipulated requirements and regulations.
"Inspections and monitoring will continue to be stepped up to ensure all goods brought into the country are accompanied by valid permits and documents and comply with the laws in force," he said.

Title: Najib arrives at Taman Duta residence to begin his house arrest (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has arrived at his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta here today to begin serving the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest.
Najib’s arrival at his Taman Duta home followed a fresh High Court order this afternoon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence at the residence until August 23, 2028.
He arrived at his residence at about 9.25pm in a silver SUV, accompanied by a convoy of several vehicles believed to be carrying security personnel, which escorted him into the compound as reporters waited outside.
A few of his supporters, who had waited here since 5pm, shouted “
Hidup Bossku
” repeatedly as Najib’s vehicle passed by.
Earlier today, High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin directed the Court Registrar to issue a new warrant of release after hearing submissions from Najib’s lawyers and Deputy Public Prosecutors.
Aslam said the new order cancelled the November 5 order and replaced it with one allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence at home.
A vehicle believed to be carrying former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrives at his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta, Kuala Lumpur on November 10, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
The fresh order came after the Attorney-General’s Chambers sought a review of the previous court order, saying clarification was needed over its wording and legal effect.
Najib had remained at Kajang Prison despite an earlier court order paving the way for his house arrest, after the AGC said implementation should be deferred pending legal clarification.
The former prime minister’s conditional royal pardon, granted on September 18, allows him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the stipulated conditions.
The arrangement followed the payment of the RM50 million fine imposed on Najib in the SRC International case.
Najib was initially sentenced to 12 years’ imprisonment and fined RM210 million in 2020. The Federal Territories Pardons Board reduced his sentence to six years and the fine to RM50 million in January 2024.

Title: Home Ministry says ready to carry out Najib’s house arrest; court order today cleared the air
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Home Ministry this evening said it is prepared to carry out a new court order today for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to be on house arrest until August 2028.
In his statement on his ministry’s readiness to execute the court’s new order, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the High Court’s latest order has helped answered legal uncertainties surrounding Najib’s house arrest.
He was referring to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur’s decision this afternoon to revoke an earlier November 6 “Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine” and to replace it with a new order that will require Najib to serve his remaining jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
The house arrest will be at Najib’s private residence at No 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta in Kuala Lumpur.
Najib, who was wearing a light blue
baju Melayu
top, was brought from Kajang Prison and was present at the court proceedings this afternoon.
On November 6, Umno had paid the RM50 million fine on behalf of Najib, as this was the condition in the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s September conditional pardon to allow him to be on house arrest in the SRC International case.
But Najib had remained in Kajang Prison since November 6, as the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) had highlighted legal uncertainties related to Najib’s house arrest.
Earlier today, the AGC filed an application at the High Court to rectify or correct the earlier court order and also to issue a new court order that would enable the house arrest, which resulted in this afternoon’s court proceedings.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail explained that the delay in implementing Najib’s house arrest previously was due to legal issues regarding interpretation of the conditional pardon order and the legal effect of the November 6 “Order of Discharge”, especially regarding the implementation of the remaining sentence via house arrest. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Saifuddin today said the Home Ministry always respects and upholds the Agong’s royal pardon decision in line with the ruler’s powers under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, and that all decisions made through constitutional channels should be respected and carried out according to the law.
Saifuddin then explained that the delay in implementing Najib’s house arrest previously was due to legal issues regarding interpretation of the conditional pardon order and the legal effect of the November 6 “Order of Discharge”, especially regarding the implementation of the remaining sentence via house arrest.
“The High Court’s decision today has clarified this issue,” he said in his statement that was titled as the government’s position on the implementation of the royal pardon involving Najib.
He said the Home Ministry respects the AGC’s position that the legal issue required clarification through a court process, adding that this approach is important to ensure each government action has a clear and valid legal basis.
“As Home Minister, I stress that the Ministry’s and the Prisons Department’s responsibility is to ensure that each decision related to the execution of sentence and detention is carried out according to the law and valid court orders,” he said in his statement.
“This case is a high-profile case which has huge political implications and public perception,” he said, urging for everyone to handle this maturely and responsibly without letting political polemics from affecting public confidence in the country’s institution.
Saifuddin concluded by saying that the federal government would continue to defend the Malay rulers’ role and position within the framework of Malaysia’s constitutional monarchy, while upholding constitutional supremacy, rule of law and the judiciary’s independence.
“These principles complete each other and are the basis for national stability,” he concluded.
While Najib will be able to serve the rest of his SRC International jail term at home until August 23, 2028, he is also facing a separate 15-year jail term in his other trial involving over RM2 billion of 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) funds.
The High Court in December 2025 had ordered Najib to immediately start serving his 15-year jail term in the 1MDB case after he completes his SRC International jail term.
Najib is currently appealing his 1MDB conviction and jail term, with the Court of Appeal yet to hear his appeal.

Title: How uncertainty over university pathways shapes Chinese youths’ choices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — For some Malaysian Chinese youths, deciding where to study after secondary school is not simply a matter of choosing a course or university.
Most of these choices are made through weighing how secure they feel about their chances of getting into their preferred programme.
In a research conducted by IMAN Research, they found that uncertainty over public university admissions, differences between pre-university pathways and concerns about access to certain courses had influenced how some the research participants approached their education.
In its recently published report,
Kami Orang Sini Juga: Chinese Youths and Democratic Belonging — The Politics of Pragmatism and Fairness
, draws on interviews with 116 Malaysian Chinese youths aged between 18 and 35 across Peninsular Malaysia.
The study found that education was one of the areas where participants’ perceptions of fairness were particularly shaped by their own experiences, expectations and accounts they had heard from others.
Some participants described choosing private education or overseas study rather than applying through the public university admission system.
One interviewee, for instance, went directly to a private university without applying through the Unit Pusat Universiti (UPU), citing concerns within the family about the chances of securing a place through the public route.
Another participant who wanted to study medicine declined an offer to pursue biotechnology and instead went to China.
The report describes these decisions as examples of how young people may seek alternatives when public pathways appear uncertain.
However, it also makes an important distinction between barriers participants personally experienced, obstacles they anticipated and accounts they had heard from family members or their wider community.
These are not the same kinds of evidence, and the researchers cautioned against treating every disappointing outcome or decision not to apply as proof of discrimination.
Matriculation and UPU are not the same
The research found that there was a recurring source of confusion among participants — the relationship between the matriculation quota and university admissions through UPU.
The report clarifies that the 90 per cent Bumiputera quota applies to entry into matriculation, not to UPU’s university selection formula.
UPU ranks applicants from STPM, matriculation and other equivalent qualifications using 90 per cent academic marks and 10 per cent co-curricular marks.
Candidates are considered according to merit, programme requirements, available places and their course preferences.
The report said the UPU pathway itself does not have an ethnic quota system.
However, the researchers noted that differences between Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) and matriculation could still raise questions about fairness.
STPM generally takes one and a half years, while the main matriculation programme takes one year.
The two pathways also use different assessment structures.
How are they different?
STPM students may progress through school, zone, district, state and national competitions, while matriculation students compete within a structure centred on inter-college competitions.
Citing figures that showed 16 per cent of matriculation students achieved a cumulative grade point average of 4.0, compared with 3.09 per cent of STPM students, the researchers suggest these differences be examined when considering how students from the two pathways are assessed
For popular courses such as medicine, pharmacy and dentistry at public universities, matriculation students accounted for more than 97 per cent of places in 2023, while STPM students made up less than 3 per cent, according to figures cited in the report.
These figures were used to illustrate differences in outcomes between the pathways, rather than establish that any individual applicant had been unfairly treated.
When students look for alternatives
The report found that family resources played an important role in determining whether young people could pursue alternatives when they felt uncertain about public education pathways.
Some could afford private universities or overseas study, while others had fewer options.
This meant that the ability to work around perceived barriers was not equally available to everyone.
The researchers also noted that concerns inherited from parents or community members could influence decisions even before a student applied for a place.
In such cases, these Chinese youths people might rule out a pathway based on what they had heard about the system, rather than on a direct experience of rejection.
The report recommends that the government make university admissions criteria, selection mechanisms and intake data more transparent and accessible.
It also calls for students to be given clearer information about how different pre-university qualifications are assessed and how they affect university options.
The researchers said differences in co-curricular opportunities between STPM and matriculation should also be reviewed, alongside clearer pathways for students holding the Unified Examination Certificate who wish to enter public universities.
Rather than redesigning the entire pre-university system, the report suggests addressing specific areas where the students face uncertainty or unequal opportunities.
Its broader concern is that when students cannot clearly understand how public education pathways work, they may make decisions based on assumptions, family experiences or perceived limitations — potentially narrowing their choices before they have fully explored them.

Title: Najib’s house arrest: What did the AGC ask the High Court to clarify today?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) today sought to ensure that Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest arrangements explicitly provided for his return to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve his separate 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) prison sentence.
In its written application, the prosecution requested that the High Court replace a November 6 discharge order with new terms clarifying Najib’s remaining SRC International sentence and his subsequent imprisonment in the 1MDB case.
The application specified that Najib should “be transferred back to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve the sentence imposed on him in the 1MDB case”.
It also sought to specify that his SRC sentence would end on August 23, 2028, with his return to prison subject to any court order then in force.
The prosecution said the 1MDB prison sentence had been directed to begin once his SRC sentence ended, arguing that “the end date of the SRC sentences must be stated with certainty”.
It explained that Najib’s payment of the RM50 million fine on November 6 discharged his liability for the fine and imprisonment for non-payment, but did not extinguish his remaining SRC prison sentence.
The AGC also argued that the earlier discharge order, which used a standard form for release upon payment of a fine, could be interpreted as releasing Najib from his remaining SRC sentence altogether.
Citing provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code governing imprisonment warrants, the prosecution said there was an urgent need for a clear order in accordance with the law.
High Court issues replacement order
High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin subsequently set aside the November 6 discharge order and issued a replacement order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
According to
Bernama,
the new order also provides for Najib’s return to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve his separate 1MDB sentence.
At the hearing, Najib’s lead counsel Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah had argued that the original discharge order was already clear, as the RM50 million fine required under the conditional royal pardon had been paid.
Speaking to reporters afterwards, Shafee welcomed the court’s clarification despite maintaining that the original order was sound.
